name: Kibana - Building SOC Dashboards & Visualizations
description: Step-by-step workflow for creating Kibana Lens visualizations and SOC dashboards from Windows event log data in Elastic SIEM.
source: CDSA Module 02: Security Monitoring & SIEM Fundamentals
notes:
Visualization workflow (Kibana Lens):
1. Dashboard → Create new dashboard → Create visualization
2. Set time range: calendar icon → Last 15 years → Apply
3. Set index pattern: windows* (or logs-*, etc.)
4. Add filters (pre-aggregation): field:value (e.g. event.code is 4625)
5. Select chart type: Table most useful for SOC monitoring
6. Configure Rows: field.keyword (e.g. user.name.keyword) → top 1000 values
7. Configure Metrics: Count
8. Add more Rows for context: host.hostname.keyword, winlog.logon.type.keyword, event.action.keyword
9. Enter KQL in search bar to further filter (e.g. NOT user.name: *$)
10. Rename columns: click field → Display name → set readable name
11. Sort results: click column header
12. Save and return → add more visualizations → Save dashboard

Field types in Kibana:
  field          → use in KQL queries
  field.keyword  → use in aggregations (Rows/Metrics in Lens)

Panel time override: gear icon → Customize time range → set absolute range
→ Useful when a single panel needs a fixed date range independent of dashboard global time.

Exclude computer accounts from auth visualizations:
  KQL: NOT user.name: *$ AND winlog.channel.keyword: Security
  (Computer accounts end with $ in Windows)

Common SOC dashboard panels:
• Failed logon attempts — all users (event 4625)
• Failed logon attempts — disabled users (4625 + SubStatus 0xC0000072)
• Failed logon attempts — admin accounts (4625 + user.name: admin*)
• RDP logons by service accounts (4624 + RemoteInteractive + user.name: svc-*)
• Local admin group membership changes (4732 / 4733 + group.name: administrators)
• Admin logon not from PAW (4624 + logon type 10, filter by source IP)
• SSH logins (Linux auth logs, user: root or unexpected accounts)
